title: Modified FOLFIRINOX for pancreatic cancer
context_label: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma or metastatic pancreatic cancer
schedule_label: Day 1 infusions, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Disconnect around day 3. Repeat every 14 days for up to 12 cycles.
schedule_summary: Day 1 infusions, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Disconnect around day 3. Repeat every 14 days for up to 12 cycles.
purpose: After surgery the aim is to reduce the chance of pancreatic cancer returning. If the cancer has spread, the aim is to control it. Ask which aim applies to you.
indication_text: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma or metastatic pancreatic cancer
administration_text: Oxaliplatin is followed by folinic acid and irinotecan. Fluorouracil runs by pump over 46 hours. This modified schedule omits the short fluorouracil injection.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and a check for nerve symptoms before each cycle.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Oxaliplatin
agents.explanation: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Cold can trigger tingling or throat discomfort. Tell the team about persistent numbness, difficulty with buttons or walking, or infusion symptoms. New breathing difficulty always needs assessment.
risks: Persistent sensory neuropathy, sometimes lasting after treatment
Rare serious lung or blood complications
consent_risks: Cold can trigger tingling or throat discomfort. Report persistent numbness, falls or difficulty fastening buttons.
Tell the nurse immediately about swelling, wheeze, faintness or trouble breathing.

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.
consent_risks: Folinic acid can intensify mouth and bowel symptoms. Report painful ulcers or diarrhoea.
Report flushing, rash or wheeze to your nurse.

agents.name: Irinotecan
agents.explanation: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about cramps, sweating or diarrhoea during the infusion. Diarrhoea starting later needs the separate written treatment and contact plan.
risks: Rare serious lung or allergic reactions
consent_risks: Report cramps, sweating or diarrhoea during the infusion immediately.
Follow your written diarrhoea plan and contact oncology without delay for diarrhoea, fever or poor fluid intake.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
agents.watch: Diarrhoea, mouth sores and skin soreness may become serious. Chest pain during the pump infusion needs emergency assessment. Unexpected severe early toxicity can occur even after DPD testing.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity
consent_risks: Chest pain or severe early toxicity
Chest pain during the pump needs emergency assessment. Contact oncology urgently for severe diarrhoea, mouth ulcers or fever.
Report painful hands or feet, line pain or a leaking pump.

common_effects.title: Eating and drinking
common_effects.text: Tell the team about nausea or reduced appetite. Call if you cannot keep fluids down.

common_effects.title: Fatigue and low counts
common_effects.text: Rest between activities. Report fever, breathlessness or unusual bleeding promptly.

common_effects.title: Nerve symptoms
common_effects.text: Report numbness or loss of balance before the next visit. Cold can trigger tingling after oxaliplatin.

serious_effects.title: Infection
serious_effects.text: Fever, shivering or sudden illness: phone oncology immediately.

serious_effects.title: Urgent symptoms
serious_effects.text: Seek urgent help for chest pain, trouble breathing or collapse.

serious_effects.title: Bowel symptoms
serious_effects.text: Ring promptly for persistent diarrhoea, dehydration or severe abdominal pain.

serious_effects.title: During irinotecan
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse about sweating, cramps or sudden diarrhoea. Later diarrhoea needs your written home plan.

evidence.title: PRODIGE 24 / CCTG PA.6 / PRODIGE 4 / ACCORD 11
evidence.interpretation: Following resection, modified FOLFIRINOX improved disease-free survival compared with gemcitabine. In metastatic disease the pivotal comparison tested standard FOLFIRINOX. It does not establish identical outcomes for the modified doses.
evidence.limitations: These are group results from the named setting. They cannot predict the benefit or side effects for an individual.

pump_care.title: Connecting the pump
pump_care.text: The day unit connects the 46-hour fluorouracil pump on day 1. Arrange disconnection by a trained team around day 3.

pump_care.title: At home with the pump
pump_care.text: Keep the line secure, dry and free of kinks. Follow your unit’s instructions for sleeping and washing. Leave disconnection and any change to the flow to your trained team.

pump_care.title: Pump or line trouble
pump_care.text: Phone the unit promptly for swelling, pain, a wet dressing, leakage or a pump that finishes much earlier or later than planned. Follow your unit’s spill instructions.
